extraction.source_locator: Fiset 1995 abstract + Table III (t1/2 ke0 5.0 light, 3.9 deep sedation)
Fiset 1995 abstract (reversal EC50 13.7 ng/mL at light, 20.6 ng/mL at deep sedation)
extraction.tier_rationale: NOT a binding constant. Fiset published the flumazenil effect-site concentration giving 50% reversal: 13.7 ng/mL at a midazolam plasma level of 160 ng/mL, rising to 20.6 ng/mL at 551 ng/mL. That rise is the surmountable signature of competitive antagonism. The light-sedation EC50 is used as the Ki SCALE (an approximation, Tier C), which is better grounded than an arbitrary constant. A human could fit a true Ki from Fiset's individual data.

known_failure_modes.condition: reversing a longer-acting benzodiazepine (antagonist clears first)
known_failure_modes.behavior: flumazenil's terminal half-life (~1 h on these kinetics) is SHORTER than midazolam's; as flumazenil clears, the receptor block wanes and sedation RELAPSES (resedation, the benzodiazepine form of renarcotization). Fiset 1995 let volunteers resedate deliberately after stopping the infusion.

extraction.tier_rationale: Flumazenil PK from 7 healthy men in 13 sessions, arterial sampling, two-stage 3-compartment means (no covariates tested), so it is absolute. ke0 from the EEG reversal of midazolam. The Ki is a reversal-EC50 scale, not a binding constant. The load-bearing behavior is resedation.

source_review.notes: V1 5.6, V2 15.93, V3 39.44 L and CL 1.12, 1.79, 0.86 L/min reproduce the table's half-lives (0.9, 11.4, 63.2 min) and Vss 61 L. The abstract's t1/2 ke0 values agree with the transcription. Against the label: clearance agrees (~0.85 vs ~1 L/h/kg), but the arterial small-V1 model gives a Cmax 2.4x the label's venous value; only clearance is comparable across sampling sites. HUMAN ITEMS: confirm Table IV, and fit a true Ki from the individual reversal data.

notes: Competitive reversal of midazolam: the apparent-Ce50 multiplier (1 + C_flumazenil/Ki) rises then falls as flumazenil clears. Now that midazolam has an executable kernel, the midazolam effect-site curve and its antagonist-adjusted equivalent are computed too, so resedation comes from both drugs' kinetics. Forward-only: never a re-dosing schedule.
